title: Mental Distress or Psychiatric Issues Reported by Teaching Staff in Schools and Institutes of Higher Learning
what_it_is: Mental Distress or Psychiatric Issues Reported by Teaching Staff in Schools and Institutes of Higher Learning

sections.label: Blended Learning implementation deferral option
sections.summary: Secondary schools and JCs could defer Blended Learning implementation to 2022 instead of Term 3 of 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For example, Secondary schools and JCs were given the option to defer the implementation of Blended Learning to 2022 instead of Term 3 of 2021, as originally planned.

sections.label: School staff seeking counsellor support
sections.summary: About 50 school staff sought MOE in-house counsellor support annually before COVID-19, rising to about 80 since 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Before COVID-19, about 50 staff from our schools sought support from MOE’s in-house counsellors annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The annual number has increased to about 80 since 2020.

sections.label: Wellness Ambassadors peer support training
sections.summary: Since September 2021, schools have nominated Wellness Ambassadors for training on basic peer support and encouraging peers to seek help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As part of a new well-being initiative since September 2021, schools have nominated Wellness Ambassadors for staff to receive training on how to provide basic peer support and encourage their peers to seek help.

sections.label: Supplementary questions on teacher well-being
sections.summary: Supplementary questions ask about steps to reduce pressures and workload, school leaders setting tone, and MOE working with unions and community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The first question is, what are the further concrete steps that MOE can take to reduce further pressures from various stakeholders, non-essential workload and support better work-life harmony, so that teachers and educators can also attend to their loved ones?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The second supplementary question is, can I suggest to the Minister that school leaders, especially, set the tone to look after the well-being of teachers, staff and educators in operationalising MOE's policies as well as meeting the schools' expectations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: My third supplementary question is, to overcome mental health and well-being issues, can I ask MOE HQ and educational institutions alike to work closely with our teachers as well as with teachers' and education's cluster of unions to better manage this issue on the ground, as we hear it is brewing; and in addition, also partnering the community and building the right societal values, especially as we move and chart the way forward in the next normal?

sections.label: Teachers' doubled workload
sections.summary: The workload for teachers has more than doubled to keep the school system going.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Not many of us realise that in order to keep our school system going, the workload for our teachers has more than doubled.

sections.label: Flexibility in scheduling and adjustments
sections.summary: Schools have flexibility to adjust scheduling, such as blended learning, and Full Subject-Based Banding roll-out will be adjusted to alleviate teacher workload.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We have given the schools some of the flexibility to adjust the scheduling, for example, the implementation of blended learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And for the Full Subject-Based Banding roll-out, we will have to make some adjustments in order to alleviate the workload on our teachers.

sections.label: Surgical breaks in term time
sections.summary: Surgical breaks are inserted into term time so teachers can get a slight break during workload spikes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The third thing in the short term that we have done is to insert what we call surgical breaks into the term time so that, in case there is a spike in the number of cases where the workload is very high, we can give our teachers a slight break.

sections.label: Systematic MOE communication with teachers
sections.summary: MOE communicates with teachers systematically, in a system of 50,000 educators and over half a million students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The fourth thing that we are doing is to make sure that when MOE communicates with our teachers, we do it systematically.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We know that this is a large system that operates with 50,000 educators, more than half a million students.

sections.label: Teachers gaining perspectives and skills
sections.summary: The wish is for teachers to acquire new perspectives, skills and connections, rolled out progressively over the long term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And not just to recharge themselves but also for them to acquire new perspectives, new skills, new connections to bring back to the school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That is my wish over the long term and we will progressively roll this out.

sections.label: Strengthening school and parent partnership
sections.summary: The partnership between schools and parents support groups should be strengthened, including parents supporting one another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That is why we need to strengthen this partnership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is the reason why I want to strengthen the partnership between the schools and the parents support groups, not so much just for the parents support groups to support the schools, but also for the parents support groups to support one another in helping one another set the correct expectations, so that we can have a strong partnership between parents and teachers in bringing up our children.

sections.label: Supporting teachers with parents and society
sections.summary: Teachers report most parents are supportive, but a small minority make huge demands, so parents, society and unions should work together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: One of the common feedback from our teachers is that most of our parents are very supportive of our teachers, but there is a small minority of parents who place a very huge demand on our teachers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, we really hope and want to work together with the parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We also want to work together with society, including the unions, so that we can better support our teachers in an all-rounded way.

sections.label: Counselling subsidies and educator carers
sections.summary: Questions are asked about cost subsidies for external counsellors and about developing a team of educator carers for teachers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Number two, I am not sure whether this was covered and I missed it: are there currently any cost subsidies that teachers can have access to when they need to see external counsellors or psychologists to deal with their stress or anxiety levels?

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And number three, in line with the perspective about rendering human support, whether MOE will consider, potentially in the long term, developing a team of Allied Educators' supporters or educator carers, to provide a listening ear and pastoral care to our teachers, so that they do not have to take the weight and the burden of all these difficult situations that they are faced with – whether it is their students' mental health, their own mental health – and they have someone to talk to?

sections.label: Allied Educators subsidy cost
sections.summary: The speaker says cost should not be an issue for the subsidy, and that trust relationships matter, not just numbers of Allied Educators and para-counsellors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The second question, on the subsidy, I do not think the cost should be an issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Yes, we are trying to increase the number of Allied Educators and also the para-counsellors but, as I have mentioned, it is not just the numbers that are important; it is also the trust relationship that needs time to build up that is important for the students and the teachers to open up.
